architecture-02.title: No CI workflow runs on a pull request into develop, so every blocking gate first sees a develop change only after it has already merged
architecture-02.survivingClaim: Narrower than the title: ci.yml alone carries the gap — its pull_request filter is [main] at :6-7 against a push filter of [main, develop] at :4-5, so no ci.yml job (the quality-scripts gates at :248-300 plus clippy :154, fmt :246, schemas :339, docs-examples :360) evaluates a develop-targeted change before it is merged. The claim does NOT extend to 'no CI workflow' — mpi-slurm.yml:5-6 names develop under pull_request and release.yml:42 / release-python.yml:26 have no base-branch filter, so all three run on a develop pull request — nor to fmt, plan-leaks and python-parity, which scripts/pre-commit evaluates pre-merge once the hook is installed; and the E4 widened diff window at check-allow-rationale.sh:368 is excluded, because ci.yml:287-289 documents the origin/main fallback as the push-event behaviour and its effect is over-scoping, not lost enforcement.
architecture-02.argument: The trigger asymmetry is real and reads exactly as the candidate says: ci.yml:4-5 gives push the branch set [main, develop] while ci.yml:6-7 gives pull_request only [main]. Every job in that file is unconditional (a grep for github.event_name over ci.yml returns no job-level condition; the only if: expressions are the MPICH cache-hit guards and the python matrix pins), so a change whose base is develop reaches the whole quality-scripts block at :248-300, clippy at :154, fmt at :246, check_schemas.sh at :339 and check-docs-examples.sh at :360 for the first time on the post-merge push, when the merge commit already carries the defect. That is the defensible residue. Two over-reaches in the title do not survive. First, the universal quantifier over workflows is false at the pin: mpi-slurm.yml:5-6 lists branches [main, develop] under pull_request, and release.yml:42 and release-python.yml:26 carry a pull_request trigger with no base-branch filter at all, so three of the eight workflows do fire on a pull request into develop. The census gates simply are not among their jobs. Second, three of the sixteen quality checks do have a pre-merge path independent of ci.yml: scripts/pre-commit runs cargo fmt --check, check-no-plan-leaks.sh and check_python_parity.py, and CONTRIBUTING.md:493 tells the contributor the hook runs the parity check automatically, so for those three the post-merge push is not the first evaluation once the hook is linked. The E4 compounding half is also stripped. The base resolution at check-allow-rationale.sh:368 and the diff window at :422 are as quoted, and on a push event BASE_REF is indeed empty so the default origin/main merge-base applies, but ci.yml:287-289 states that fallback as the intended push-event behaviour and the fetch-depth rationale at :256-257 provisions for it; the consequence is a wider scan window, which over-scopes rather than under-enforces, so it is not an enforcement gap. I found no repository text at the pin that states the develop pull_request exclusion as a deliberate choice: CONTRIBUTING.md:386 documents branching from main, which explains why the filter covers main, but develop never appears in its submission flow, and the develop cadence prose in docs/design/testing-architecture.md:499 sits under a section headed as a proposed standard and itself assumes the smoke and PR-fast tiers run on every push and every PR. Absent such a statement there is no deliberate-and-documented or cost-accepted-by-rule basis, and the fix shape stays an in-place amendment of the trigger list, which strengthens rather than weakens a gate.

architecture-03.title: The invariance-shuffle workflow cannot compile the test target it dispatches, and the automatic suite skips the same tests, so the declaration-order-invariance shuffle matrix has no executable path in CI
architecture-03.survivingClaim: Both invariance-shuffle.yml run lines (:34 and :55) omit cobre-sddp's own test-support feature, so the parity target they name fails to compile at the pin (lib.rs:46-47 gates pub mod test_support, which parity.rs:752-1461 uses unconditionally, and Cargo.toml:77 only enables cobre-core's like-named feature): the residue is that the FULL_SHUFFLE_PERMUTATIONS sweep behind the bare ignore at parity.rs:139-163 and its CLP twin at :298-322 has no working invocation in the tree, NOT that declaration-order invariance is unverified in CI, since the i = 0 permutation folded into each parity_hash_<case> test (parity.rs:28-32) runs on both backends via ci.yml:114 and ci.yml:233 under NON_SOLVER_FEATURES (ci.yml:32), which carries both slow-tests and test-support.
architecture-03.argument: Verified at the pin. invariance-shuffle.yml:34 passes only slow-tests and :55 only clp plus slow-tests, while the parity target references cobre_sddp::test_support::fill_consistent_basis at crates/cobre-sddp/tests/parity.rs:894 from inside the ungated mod determinism opened at :752, with further unconditional uses at :1303, :1437 and :1461. crates/cobre-sddp/src/lib.rs:46-47 gates pub mod test_support on cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support")), and the library is compiled without cfg(test) when an integration test links it, so that module is absent unless the crate's own feature is named on the command line. crates/cobre-sddp/Cargo.toml:55 declares test-support = ["cobre-core/test-support"], and the dev-dependency at :77 enables cobre-core's like-named feature, a different package's, which does not turn on cobre-sddp's; no self dev-dependency exists in the manifest, so nothing enables it implicitly under -p cobre-sddp. Both dispatched jobs therefore fail while compiling the named target, before any shuffle test is selected, and neither step sets continue-on-error, so the failure would fail the dispatched run. The reason no automatic path surfaces it is that ci.yml:32 NON_SOLVER_FEATURES carries test-support and features unify workspace-wide by name, so ci.yml:114 and the CLP nextest step at ci.yml:233 compile the same target successfully. The two shuffle run lines are the only invocations in the tree that omit the feature, which is why this is an amend-in-place defect confined to those lines rather than a missing gate or a new framework. I narrow the consequence the title draws. parity.rs:28-32 records that each parity_hash_<case> test folds in the i = 0 permutation, and those tests carry the slow-tests cfg_attr form that both ci.yml:114 and ci.yml:233 enable, so single-permutation declaration-order invariance is verified automatically on both backends. What has no working invocation is the FULL_SHUFFLE_PERMUTATIONS sweep behind the bare ignore at parity.rs:139-163 and its CLP twin at :298-322, which cargo test cannot reach without --include-ignored. I also correct the candidate's scope: the bare-ignore shuffle set exists in both the highs-gated module and the clp-gated module, so the second run line is broken for its own copy of the set, not for the one the candidate anchored.

architecture-04.title: The CLI template mirror is guarded in one direction only: a file added to the canonical example deck but not to the embedded list leaves both guards green while cobre init ships an incomplete case
architecture-04.survivingClaim: No guard in the corpus compares the canonical examples/1dtoy/ file SET against either hand-maintained enumeration (build.rs TEMPLATE_FILES at :16, templates.rs DTOY1_FILES), so the single escaping edit is ADDING a presence-discovered optional input file to the canonical deck without changing any already-embedded file's bytes; canonical deletion is caught by the expect at templates.rs:210 and modification (including any addition that config.json references) by the assert_eq! at templates.rs:212, and check-docs-examples.sh:113 is conceded to meet its own declared CLI-output-shape contract rather than being a deficient mirror guard, with the resulting drift being divergence from the documented canonical deck rather than a broken or unrunnable init output.
architecture-04.argument: Three hand-maintained lists describe the same deck at the pin, and two of the three edges between them are machine-enforced. build.rs fails the build when a TEMPLATE_FILES entry (:16 to :28) has no file under crates/cobre-cli/templates/1dtoy/, because fs::copy at build.rs:49 panics at :50; and include_bytes! over DTOY1_FILES fails to compile when an entry has no OUT_DIR copy, so enumeration-to-disk and enumeration-to-enumeration both hold. The edge the candidate names is genuinely open. test_1dtoy_embedded_files_match_canonical_source at templates.rs:204 iterates template.files, so its domain is the embedded set, and git ls-tree over examples/1dtoy/ and crates/cobre-cli/templates/1dtoy/ at the pin shows corresponding trees only because the two cardinalities happen to agree. Nothing in the corpus reads the canonical directory listing. I narrow on three over-reaches. First, check-docs-examples.sh:113 is not a template-mirror guard: its header at :1 to :8 and :20 to :23 declares it a CLI on-disk-output-shape gate, and the configured EXPECTED_INPUT_FILES=11 at :32 pins what cobre init WRITES, which is the embedded cardinality, so the gate meets its own stated contract and the defect is a missing assertion in the corpus rather than a deficient gate. Second, the escaping edit is narrower than any file addition: deleting a canonical file trips the std::fs::read expect at templates.rs:210, modifying one trips the assert_eq! at templates.rs:212, and an addition that is referenced from an already-embedded file trips that same byte compare on config.json. What escapes is specifically an additive input file the loader discovers by PRESENCE, which crates/cobre-io/src/validation/structural.rs:11 to :14 records without erroring, its InputFile registry listing many optional paths the 1dtoy deck does not carry. Third, shipping an incomplete case overstates the impact: the materialized deck remains the previous self-consistent deck and still runs, which is why the run half of the same gate stays green, so what diverges silently is the equivalence between what cobre init materializes and the canonical deck the docs point at. One correction to the candidate evidence: its grep output asserts that no script or workflow mentions examples/1dtoy, but ci.yml:578 names it in a step comment and the notebook step at ci.yml:581 executes the quickstart against that deck. That is a consumer, not a set comparison, so the load-bearing claim survives. The amend-in-place shape is feasible, since the script cd's to REPO_ROOT at :30 to :31 and already holds the template name at :33, and replacing a count literal with a set comparison strengthens the gate rather than loosening it, which rule 6b requires. One caveat on that shape: a strict set-EQUALITY assert would also forbid non-input files in a canonical deck, and examples/4ree/README.md shows the repo allows exactly that for a sibling deck.

architecture-05.survivingClaim: Only the `[lints.clippy]` table at `crates/cobre-python/Cargo.toml:50-55`, including `unwrap_used = deny`, is evaluated by no step at the pin, and the gap is a documented-but-uncarried contributor obligation rather than an unrecognised blind spot: both clippy runs (`ci.yml:154`, `ci.yml:221`) are `--workspace` and the crate is excluded at `Cargo.toml:21-23`, while `CONTRIBUTING.md:216` already states that clippy for this crate needs `--manifest-path` because the workspace-wide invocations skip it, yet neither the contributor checklist at `CONTRIBUTING.md:386` nor the release checklist at `:602-604` carries that command and `scripts/pre-commit` runs no clippy. Excluded from the residue: the sibling `[lints.rust]` table at `:46-48`, which IS evaluated and blocking, because `RUSTFLAGS: -Dwarnings` at `ci.yml:11` escalates `missing_docs` in the two python-job steps that compile the crate (`:559` maturin develop, `:567` cargo test). Also excluded: any live violation, since the ten `.unwrap()` uses all sit under the `#[cfg(test)]` allow at `errors.rs:358-359`.
architecture-05.contractCited: `clippy::all` and `clippy::pedantic` at `warn` level, zero warnings in CI
architecture-05.argument: Verified exhaustively at the pin. A grep for clippy across `.github` and `scripts` returns only two invocations, `ci.yml:154` in the `clippy` job at `:116` and `ci.yml:221` in the `clp` job, both `--workspace --all-targets` with `-D warnings`, neither carrying `--manifest-path`; the single `--manifest-path` in the whole enforcement layer is the `cargo test` at `ci.yml:567`, and `scripts/pre-commit` contains no clippy at all. Because `Cargo.toml:21-23` excludes the crate, no step anywhere drives the clippy driver over it, so the `[lints.clippy]` table at `crates/cobre-python/Cargo.toml:50-55` (`all` and `pedantic` at warn, `unwrap_used` at deny, `expect_used` and `panic` at warn) is evaluated nowhere, while `CLAUDE.md:21` makes zero clippy warnings in CI non-negotiable per `:17` and `CLAUDE.md:19` places this crate inside the lint regime with exactly one named override, `unsafe_code`, rather than outside it. Three dismissal routes were tested and all fail. Sanctioned-advisory does not reach it: the sanctioned workspace exclusion at `Cargo.toml:18-23`, expanded at `ARCHITECTURE.md:241-245`, justifies non-membership by the interpreter requirement, yet the python job already has an interpreter and already compiles this exact manifest at `:559` and `:567`, so the sanction covers the exclusion and not the absence of a lint pass. Premise-false-at-pin fails because the grep is exhaustive. Deliberate-and-documented comes closest and still fails, and it is what forces the narrowing: `CONTRIBUTING.md:214-217` states that `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy` for this crate need `--manifest-path` because the workspace-wide invocations skip it. That records the mechanical skip and assigns a manual remedy; it records no decision to leave the crate unlinted, and the two checklists that would operationalise it, the contributor steps at `:386` and the release steps at `:602-604`, list only the `--workspace` commands, so the documented obligation has no carrier. The residue is narrower than the title in two ways, both in the surviving claim. First, the sibling `[lints.rust]` table at `:46-48` is not part of it, since `RUSTFLAGS: -Dwarnings` is workflow-level env at `ci.yml:11` and `missing_docs` is therefore evaluated and blocking in both python-job compiles of the crate. Second, the gap is a documented-but-uncarried obligation, not an unrecognised blind spot. Enforcement strength is blocking because the anchored subject is the pair of clippy steps, which are exit-code-bearing under `-D warnings`; the defect is their scope, not their strength, and a negative grep is never evidence for unwired. No live breach exists at the pin: all ten `.unwrap()` occurrences sit in `crates/cobre-python/src/errors.rs`, under the `#[cfg(test)]` module whose allow is at `:359`, with the crate-level carve-out at `lib.rs:17`. The asymmetry the candidate names also holds: the `allow(clippy::...)` suppressions spread across eight files under `crates/cobre-python/src/` are already in scope of the blocking E4 rationale gate at `ci.yml:292`, whose pathspec `crates/*/src/*.rs` at `check-allow-rationale.sh:422` crosses directory separators by that script's own comment at `:419-421`, so a new suppression there must carry a written rationale for a lint no job runs. That is amend-in-place, adds no gate framework and no one-consumer abstraction, so none of the layering brief section 3 triggers fires. This is the first adjudication of the inbound cli-python NH8 handoff and is argued from the tree.

over-engineering-00.title: The MPICH Cache/Build/Set step triple is copied byte-for-byte eight times inside ci.yml, with two near-variants in mpi-slurm.yml and release-mpi.yml and no composite action anywhere under .github/

over-engineering-00.survivingClaim: Inside ci.yml alone, the Cache/Build/Set MPICH triple at 43-68 recurs byte-identically in seven further jobs (81-106, 124-149, 174-199, 310-335, 371-396, 462-487, 516-541) with no in-file rationale, and that intra-file eightfold copy is the un-factored duplication; the mpi-slurm.yml (56-83) and release-mpi.yml (67-99) variants are excluded from the shared-abstraction target because each file documents the reason for its own shape at release-mpi.yml 65-66 and 1-19 and via the container image mpi-slurm.yml pins to MPICH_VERSION.
over-engineering-00.argument: Every load-bearing fact holds at the pin. Reading ci.yml at 43-68 and comparing that region against 81-106, 124-149, 174-199, 310-335, 371-396, 462-487 and 516-541 yields no difference in all seven comparisons, so the Cache MPICH / Build MPICH from source / Set MPICH environment triple exists as eight byte-identical copies inside one file, one each in the check (35), test (73), clippy (116), clp (166), schemas (302), docs (363), coverage (454) and python (504) jobs. A tree listing of .github at the pin returns the single entry workflows, so no composite action exists today. Nothing in the eight regions states why the copies are inline, and the same file does record a deliberate non-duplication decision in prose at 361 for the docs job, so the silence around the triple is not a documented choice and no sanctioned item, rule or accepted-cost clause covers it. The triple is setup inside jobs that are themselves blocking, hence the blocking strength: the copies are the environment those blocking jobs need, not a gate of their own. Rule 8 exempts this subject from the one-consumer objection, so a shared action would follow present consumers rather than anticipate any, and nothing conflicts with the layering. I narrow on the candidate's out-of-file half. The two variants are not undocumented divergences. release-mpi.yml states at 65-66 that only headers and libmpi.so are needed at compile time because the user's own MPICH loads at runtime, which is exactly why its Set step at 95-99 omits the LD_LIBRARY_PATH export that ci.yml makes at 68; its header at 1-19 and the brew branch at 101-104 are the reason all three of its steps carry the matrix.mpi_source guard at 68, 76 and 96. mpi-slurm.yml (triple 56-83) runs its MPI inside the container image pinned to MPICH_VERSION, so the runner likewise needs no library path. Folding those two documented shapes into guard and library-path inputs of one shared action, as the fixShape proposes, converts reasons each file already explains into parameters and reshapes the release-critical path; that half is over-reach. The defensible residue is the eightfold identical copy inside ci.yml.

over-engineering-01.title: The MPICH version literal 4.2.3 has three independent owners in the SLURM image path (workflow env, Dockerfile ARG default, pushed image tag) and no build-arg links them, so the tag can name a version the image was not built from
over-engineering-01.survivingClaim: At the pin the base image has two unlinked version decisions, not three: the ARG default at tests/slurm/Dockerfile.base:42 fixes what is compiled and slurm-base-image.yml:14 fixes the tag pushed at :41, with no build-args key in the :35-44 build step joining them, so bumping either alone publishes an image whose tag misnames its MPICH; the pushed tag is not a separate owner because :41 interpolates :14. A separate third literal at tests/slurm/Dockerfile:15 decides what the cluster image builds FROM, because neither build block in tests/slurm/docker-compose.yml passes args, which is why the tag pulled at mpi-slurm.yml:106 is not the tag consumed.
over-engineering-01.argument: Every load-bearing premise holds at the pin. The build-push step at slurm-base-image.yml:35-44 declares context, file, push, tags, cache-from and cache-to and no build-args key, and a grep for build-args over .github at the pin returns nothing at all, so the MPICH version actually compiled is decided solely by the ARG default at tests/slurm/Dockerfile.base:42 while the tag pushed at :41 interpolates env.MPICH_VERSION from :14. No expression joins them and no file under scripts/ mentions MPICH_VERSION, so nothing verifies that the published tag names the version inside the image; editing :42 alone still fires the path filter at :5-8 and republishes a differently built image under the unchanged tag. I narrow the title on two points. First, the workflow env and the pushed tag are not independent owners: :41 derives the tag from :14 by interpolation, so they are one decision and the title over-counts them as two.
